title: Shank out
description: Fastener grip against the complete clamped stack, the eye riding as a loudly-marked placeholder.

checks.label: shank out, NAS6403U11D
checks.guidance: clamped column minus grip. Negative means the end of the full cylindrical shank sits proud of the nut bearing face, so the nut would engage incomplete threads -- which JPS00094 Rev C section 5.5.5 forbids outright ('The nut, nutplate, insert, part body, etc., shall not engage any incomplete threads of the bolt shank'). COMPLETE SINCE 2026-09-15 (handoff stack_fable_audit): the pitch-link eye and the NAS77A3-015A flange, this column's two missing members, are now terms, so the verdict speaks for the modelled joint -- but THREE of the five column terms are unverified (the eye a loudly-marked placeholder whose bearing identity needs the 213862-002 drawing, the bushing an operator reading, the washer a workbook band), so read the verdict with `worst_confidence: untraced` in view. It PASSES worst case by 0.1098 mm (column at min 17.8390 against grip at max 17.7292) -- a thin margin that a wrong placeholder erases: if the eye were the WIDE MS14103-3 (11.05/11.10) the check would read +4.0 mm and the cotter-hole check would go negative, which is one of the reasons the narrow bearing is the credible candidate. This guidance is a copy of the referenced stack's own, kept in step by hand.

provenance.pinned_by: tests/test_topology_conversions.py -- every field of the folded interval must equal that check's, exactly.

notes: The selection is a lasso, not a path: traverse() re-orders it. The chain walks `fastener_grip` AGAINST its authored orientation (shank_full_dia_end -> head_bearing_face, sign -1) then the five clamped edges WITH their authored orientation (sign +1 each), so the total is `clamped_stack_sourced - fastener_grip` -- the same sign convention the referenced check's own term list uses (path term default +1, `bolt_grip_11` sign -1). No sign is authored anywhere in this file; both come off the graph.

This study reproduces stack path `clamped_stack_sourced` (bushing + eye + flange + pitch-plate lug + washer) as a strict subset of its own selection -- the five clamped edges alone, walked head-to-tail, are exactly that path's own term list.
Its description said 'The pitch-link eye is an excluded term' until 2026-09-15 (stack_fable_audit); the eye is a term now, a loudly-marked placeholder -- see the edge and the referenced element.
